The *Billiyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like many short poems in this collection, it preserves the biographical reflections and karmic history of an elder disciple of the Buddha [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are identified by SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis reveals widespread formulaic reuse within the Pali canon: DharmaNexus records 72 matching passages distributed across 33 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, verses spanning §4.2–9.1 exhibit extensive repetition with several other fruit-offering apadānas, showing closest alignment with the *Kāsumāraphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 505), *Pādaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 507), *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 386), *Labujaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 469), and *Kosambaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 515) [DharmaNexus].
